questions.question_text: Which correlation coefficient denotes an inverse relationship?
questions.explanation: Correlation ranges from -1 (perfect negative/inverse) through 0 (none) to +1 (perfect positive). Motulsky, Intuitive Biostatistics, pg 185.

questions.question_text: The lifetime prevalence of OCD is
questions.explanation: Lifetime prevalence of OCD varies from about 1 to 3%. New Oxford Textbook of Psychiatry, Vol 1, pg 823.

questions.question_text: What is the risk of neural tube defects with sodium valproate in pregnancy?
questions.explanation: Valproate in the first trimester carries a 1–4% risk of neural tube defects (approximately 1 in 50). Synopsis of Psychiatry, 10th edn, pg 1114.

questions.question_text: A 34 year-old woman with schizophrenia has apathy, fatigue, abdominal bloating and constipation. Which electrolyte disturbance?
questions.explanation: Hypercalcemia causes 'stones, groans and psychic moans' (renal stones, abdominal pain/constipation, depression/fatigue). Oxford Handbook of Clinical Medicine, 7th edn, pg 672.

questions.question_text: You want to use an α2-agonist in a 36 year-old with a tendency to low blood pressure. Which do you choose?
questions.explanation: Lofexidine and clonidine are α2-agonists; lofexidine causes less hypotension than clonidine. NICE guidelines, 2007.

questions.question_text: Visual field defects are seen with:
questions.explanation: Vigabatrin is associated with bilateral visual field defects. Wilton et al. BMJ. 1999;319:1165–1166.

questions.question_text: A woman who had herpes encephalitis develops severe carbohydrate craving, weight gain and increased sexual drive. Likely diagnosis:
questions.explanation: Klüver-Bucy syndrome is associated with overeating, hypersexuality, placidity and hyperorality after temporal lobe damage. Moore, Textbook of Clinical Neuropsychiatry, 2nd edn, pg 127.

questions.question_text: The risk of heart failure in patients with coronary artery disease and depression compared to those without depression is:
questions.explanation: The risk of heart failure in CAD patients with depression is 16.4 per 100 versus 3.6 per 100 in those without depression, giving an approximate 5:1 ratio. May et al. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2009;53:1440–1447.

questions.question_text: The last stage according to Prochaska and DiClemente’s model of behaviour change is:
questions.explanation: In the maintenance stage the new behaviours (e.g., abstinence) are sustained beyond six months. Handbook of Alcoholism, 2000, Zernig et al., pp 99–100.

questions.question_text: A 19-year-old pregnant girl asks for the best time to undergo opiate withdrawal during pregnancy:
questions.explanation: Withdrawal risks miscarriage and distress; guidelines recommend starting methadone early and continuing throughout pregnancy rather than abrupt withdrawal in a single trimester. Day & George. Adv Psychiatric Treat. 2005;11:253–261.

questions.question_text: A patient with moderate depression has had a partial response to fluoxetine but still has insomnia. Useful augmentation is:
questions.explanation: NICE (2009) advises Lithium, Mirtazapine, Mianserin, or antipsychotics as augmenting agents. For persistent insomnia, Mirtazapine’s sedative effect is advantageous. Depression in Adults. NICE 2009.

questions.question_text: In anorexia nervosa, which is more likely?
questions.explanation: Anorexia nervosa commonly shows a 'euthyroid sick' pattern with low T3. Other findings include raised GH and cortisol, low oestrogen, and leucopenia.

questions.question_text: What type of graph is shown (survival curves for smokers vs non-smokers developing depression)?
questions.explanation: This is a plot of survival function over time, showing the proportion of subjects free of depression at each time point—a Kaplan–Meier curve.

questions.question_text: In the above survival graph, values along the Y axis refer to:

options.text: Time to onset of major depression

questions.explanation: A Kaplan–Meier survival curve’s Y axis shows the probability of remaining event-free—in this case, not developing depression.

questions.question_text: When do the two groups (smokers and non-smokers) have similar probability of developing depression?
questions.explanation: The two survival curves are closest (nearly overlapping) between 2 and 4 years before diverging, indicating similar probabilities then.

questions.question_text: What type of graph is shown (BPRS scores over time, shared vs standard care)?
questions.explanation: This diagram shows medians, quartiles, and ranges for BPRS scores at each time point for each group—a box-and-whisker plot.

questions.question_text: In that box-and-whisker plot, the box itself represents:
questions.explanation: The box spans the interquartile range (from the 25th to the 75th percentile) in a box plot.

questions.question_text: In that box plot, the vertical lines (‘whiskers’) represent:
questions.explanation: The whiskers connect the minimum and maximum observed values, showing the full range.

questions.question_text: From the shared care box plots, what can be deduced?

options.text: Shared care is better than standard at 12 months
Shared care is better than standard at 6 months
It is not possible to deduce from the information provided
There is no difference between shared and standard care
Standard care is better than shared at 12 months

correct_answer.text: It is not possible to deduce from the information provided

correct_answers.text: It is not possible to deduce from the information provided

questions.explanation: Box plots display descriptive summaries only. They do not provide inferential statistics or significance testing to draw conclusions on group differences.

questions.question_text: In the suicide-in-dementia study, the strength of the design is:

options.text: Can evaluate multiple outcomes of a single exposure

questions.explanation: A case–control study is especially suited for rare outcomes, such as suicide in dementia, because it starts with identified cases and compares them to controls.

questions.question_text: The particular strength of the methodology in the suicide-in-dementia study is:

options.text: The control group selected for this study
Psychiatrists blind to the study purpose
The high percentage of forms returned by the Psychiatrist
All the suicides during the specificed time period were included in this study

correct_answer.text: The high percentage of forms returned by the Psychiatrist

correct_answers.text: The high percentage of forms returned by the Psychiatrist

questions.explanation: By including all suicides during the specified nine-year period, the study minimized selection bias among cases.

questions.question_text: Controls in the suicide-in-dementia study were more likely to be selected if they were:

options.text: Mental-illness patients who did not commit suicide
Patients with another mental illness who completed suicide
People with no mental illness who completed suicide
Patients with dementia who did not commit suicide

correct_answer.text: Patients with another mental illness who completed suicide

correct_answers.text: Patients with another mental illness who completed suicide

questions.explanation: Controls were gender-matched individuals who died by suicide but did not have a diagnosis of dementia (i.e., had other psychiatric diagnoses).

questions.question_text: The commonest method used by dementia patients to commit suicide was:
questions.explanation: Among dementia suicide cases, 30 of 118 (28%) used self-poisoning, making it the single most frequent method.

questions.question_text: Which method was significantly less common in dementia patients than in controls?
questions.explanation: Hanging occurred in 17% of dementia cases versus 30% of controls; the odds ratio 0.45 (95% CI 0.26–0.78) is <1 and CI excludes 1, indicating significantly lower use among dementia patients.

questions.question_text: If the UK population is 55 million, the annual incidence of suicide over the nine-year study (45 012 deaths) is approximately:
questions.explanation: 45012 suicides over 9 years equals ~5000/year. Divided by 55 000 000 gives ~0.00009 (0.009%) ≈1 per thousand per year.

questions.question_text: Screening terminally ill patients with ‘Are you depressed?’ vs a structured interview: Prevalence of depression in the sample?
questions.explanation: Prevalence = total with depression ÷ total sample = 25/74 ≈ 33.8% ≈33%.

questions.question_text: From that table, the sensitivity of the screening question is:
questions.explanation: Sensitivity = true positives ÷ all with disease = 11/25 = 44%.

questions.question_text: From that table, the specificity of the screening question is:
questions.explanation: Specificity = true negatives ÷ all without disease = 40/49 ≈ 81.6% ≈82%.

questions.question_text: Proportion of those who screened positive who actually were depressed (positive predictive value)?
questions.explanation: PPV = true positives ÷ all positives = 11/20 = 55%.

questions.question_text: Proportion of those who were depressed who screened positive (another sensitivity measure)?
questions.explanation: This again is sensitivity = 11/25 = 44%.

questions.question_text: Negative predictive value of the screening question?
questions.explanation: NPV = true negatives ÷ all negatives = 40/54 ≈ 74%.

questions.question_text: Reversible dementia scenario: 55 y o lady with memory disturbance, early morning headache improving by day, facial nerve palsy. Treatment?
questions.explanation: Early morning headaches and focal palsy suggest a brain tumour; treatment is surgical evacuation. Larner AJ. Pract Neurol. 2009;9:80–84.

questions.question_text: Reversible dementia scenario: 45 y o lady with alcohol problems, ataxia, nystagmus, asterixis. Treatment?
questions.explanation: Presentation suggests Wernicke’s encephalopathy; treat with Thiamine.

questions.question_text: Reversible dementia scenario: 65 y o lady with cognitive impairment, urinary incontinence, ataxia. Treatment?
questions.explanation: Normal pressure hydrocephalus triad (gait disturbance, dementia, incontinence) is treated by ventriculoperitoneal shunting.

questions.question_text: Rating scales in dementia: Used for differential diagnosis?
questions.explanation: CAMDEX (Cambridge Mental Disorders of the Elderly Examination) and AGECAT cover major diagnoses in old-age psychiatry.

questions.question_text: Rating scales in dementia: Used to assess progression of dementia with treatment?
questions.explanation: CAPE (Clifton Assessment Procedure for the Elderly) provides an estimate of severity and can track progression.

questions.question_text: Rating scales in dementia: Used as a screening test?
questions.explanation: The MMSE, Addenbrooke’s ACE, and the orientation section of CAPE are used as brief screening tools for dementia.

questions.question_text: Research methods: In an RCT of Xanomeline vs chlorpromazine (500 per arm), 200 respond to X, 300 to CPZ; 100 X and 50 CPZ develop EPS. Experimental event rate (EER) for clinical response in the Xanomeline group?
questions.explanation: EER = responders in experimental arm ÷ total experimental = 200/500 = 0.40 = 40%.

questions.question_text: In that trial, control event rate (CER) for clinical response in chlorpromazine group is:
questions.explanation: CER = responders in control arm ÷ total control = 300/500 = 0.60 = 60%.

questions.question_text: Absolute risk reduction (ARR) for clinical response using Xanomeline is:
Number needed to treat (NNT) for Xanomeline is:
EER for extrapyramidal side-effects in the Xanomeline group is:
questions.explanation: EPS EER = cases in experimental arm ÷ total experimental = 100/500 = 0.20 = 20%.

questions.question_text: CER for EPS in the chlorpromazine group is:
questions.explanation: EPS CER = cases in control arm ÷ total control = 50/500 = 0.10 = 10%.

questions.question_text: Absolute risk increase (ARI) for EPS using Xanomeline is:
Number needed to harm (NNH) for EPS with Xanomeline is:
Movement disorder: 65 y o lady with short-stepping gait, small cramped handwriting, vertical gaze problem. Diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Progressive supranuclear palsy presents with vertical gaze palsy, Parkinsonism with small-step gait, and handwriting changes. Lishman’s Organic Psychiatry, 4th edn, pg 776.

questions.question_text: A 15 y o boy develops sudden non-repetitive arm movements 6 months after pharyngitis. Diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Sydenham’s chorea follows Group A streptococcal infection by weeks to months, producing rapid, irregular, involuntary movements. Companion to Psychiatric Studies, 7th edn, pg 492.

questions.question_text: A 45 y o man with progressive memory loss and wife reports electric-shock-like muscle jerks. Diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease features rapidly progressive dementia with myoclonus (shock-like jerks). Patients often die within months. Textbook of Clinical Neuropsychiatry, 2nd edn, pg 127.

questions.question_text: A 37 y o woman has involuntary blinking and chin thrusting, intact cognition, uses gum to conceal movements. Diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Meige’s syndrome (oral-facio-dystonia) presents with involuntary blinking and facial movements that patients may mask with chewing gum. Moore, Textbook of Clinical Neuropsychiatry, 2nd edn, pg 127.

questions.question_text: A 23 year old woman brings her boyfriend who always asks her before he does anything which is causing some irritation to her. He always tries to please his colleagues by accepting to do things even though he may struggle with overload of work.
questions.explanation: Dependent personality disorder features submissiveness, reliance on others for decisions, and difficulty taking responsibility. Prevalence ~0.7%. Freud’s oral stage fixation.

questions.question_text: A young lady with too much make up and has a seductive way of dressing. She is very emotional when criticised.
questions.explanation: Histrionic personality disorder is characterized by attention-seeking, dramatic, and sexually seductive behaviour with shallow emotions.

questions.question_text: A 40 year old stock broker was referred to the community alcohol team due to problems at work. He is upset that he had to wait for up to half an hour before seeing the doctor and had shouted twice at the receptionist. On seeing the doctor, he mentions that he is possibly the best in the business, which has upset some of the partners in their firm and had denied them the bonus that they deserved. His reason for drinking in excess is due his employer's lack of appreciation of his talents rather than any other reason. He is upset when the Doctor refuses to see him on a daily basis, and feel that psychiatrists are 'failed doctors' and refuses to come back to the clinic.
questions.explanation: Narcissistic personality disorder features grandiosity, need for admiration, lack of empathy, and sensitivity to criticism.

questions.question_text: Study of PTSD in illegal immigrants with no sampling frame. Sampling method?
questions.explanation: Snowball sampling recruits hidden or hard-to-reach populations by asking initial subjects to identify others in the target group.

questions.question_text: Study of metabolic syndrome in antipsychotic-treated patients. He first stratifies into inpatients, outpatients, CMHT. Sampling method?
questions.explanation: Stratified random sampling divides the population into strata (inpatient, outpatient, community teams) and samples each subgroup to ensure representation.

questions.question_text: To survey prevalence of depression across all UK primary-care attendees, they randomly pick representative primary-care authorities and survey all patients there. Sampling?
questions.explanation: Cluster sampling selects groups (clusters) such as regional authorities then surveys all members within selected clusters.

questions.question_text: Research nurse conducts qualitative study of mentally ill parents’ experience with teenage children. Sampling?
questions.explanation: Convenience sampling is common in qualitative research when participants are selected by willingness and accessibility.

questions.question_text: A baby born with facial abnormalities (small palpebral fissures, thin upper lip, smooth philtrum). Diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Foetal Alcohol Syndrome is characterized by characteristic facial anomalies, growth retardation, and central nervous system abnormalities due to in utero alcohol exposure.

questions.question_text: A baby born with facial abnormalities.
questions.explanation: Children with Fetal Alcohol Syndrome have Facial anomalies, Growth retardation and abnormal CNS development.

questions.question_text: High pitched cry and irritability in baby following birth.
questions.explanation: Neonatal withdrawal from heroin in the new born can cause high pitched crying, seizures, coma, irritability, tremor, sneezing and diarrhoea.

questions.question_text: Some mild irritability and changes in tone are seen.
questions.explanation: Neonatal withdrawal from Amphetamines is associated with irritability, hypotonic, respiratory distress in the new born.

questions.question_text: A 20 year old woman is brought to you by dominating parents. She has been losing weight and her mother is concerned about this. Her father feels that she is trying to push her mother away because she refuses to put the heating on in the house, as she says she is very sensitive to it.
questions.explanation: Major clinical signs include weight loss (often accompanied by an increased appetite), anxiety, intolerance to heat, hair loss, weakness, hyperactivity, irritability, apathy, depression, polyuria, polydipsia, delirium, tremor, and sweating. Additionally, patients may present with a variety of symptoms such as palpitations and arrhythmias (notably atrial fibrillation), shortness of breath (dyspnea), loss of libido, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhoea. Long term untreated hyperthyroidism can lead to osteoporosis. In the elderly, these classical symptoms may not be present.

questions.question_text: A 16 year old girl is brought in by her parents who are concerned that she counts the calories in everything she eats and exercises excessively. Her BMI is 16.5.
questions.explanation: Anorexia nervosa is a psychiatric illness that describes an eating disorder characterized by extremely low body weight and body image distortion with an obsessive fear of gaining weight. Individuals with anorexia nervosa are known to control body weight commonly through the means of voluntary starvation, calorie counting, excessive exercise, or other weight control measures such as diet pills or diuretic drugs.

questions.question_text: A young girl is brought to you by her parents because they are concerned about her recent weight loss and also that she has fatty foul-smelling stools. You notice on examination that she has mouth ulcers and angular stomatitis.
questions.explanation: The diarrhoea characteristic of coeliac disease is pale, voluminous and malodorous. Abdominal pain and cramping, bloatedness with abdominal distension (thought to be due to fermentative production of bowel gas), angular stomatitis and mouth ulcers may be present.

questions.question_text: A 40 year old man with Alcohol Dependence Syndrome doesn't want to stop drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Pre-contemplation: Not currently considering change; motivational interviewing involves validating lack of readiness, clarifying that decision is theirs, encouraging re-evaluation of current behavior, and encouraging self-exploration rather than action.

questions.question_text: A 51 year old woman with Alcoholic liver disease wants to stop drinking alcohol on her birthday in 2 weeks time.
questions.explanation: Preparation: Some experience with change and are trying to change; planning to act within 1 month. Techniques include identifying and assisting in problem solving regarding obstacles, helping patient identify social support, verifying that patient has underlying skills for behavior change, and encouraging small initial steps.

questions.question_text: A 57 year old man has not any alcohol for the past 15 years after having had a history of significant alcohol problems prior to that.
questions.explanation: Relapse: Resumption of old behaviors; involves evaluating trigger for relapse, reassessing motivation and barriers, and planning stronger coping strategies.

questions.question_text: A 4 year girl who is very aggressive and disruptive in school. She has hit one of the other pupils.
questions.explanation: Parent skills training is indicated here as positive parenting is known to have good outcomes.

questions.question_text: An 8 year old boy presents with repeated eye blinking, grimacing, using swear words repeatedly and also obscene gestures.
questions.explanation: Low dose antipsychotics have been shown to be effective in severe Tourettes syndrome.

questions.question_text: A 16 year old girl presents with low mood, anhedonia and suicidal ideations.
questions.explanation: SSRIs have been suggested as the first line of treatment of antidepressant medication in adolescent depression who prefer medication.

questions.question_text: A patient with colour visual problems
questions.explanation: Early symptoms of digitalis intoxication include visual disturbances such as unusual colour visions with objects appearing yellowish to green and blue halos around lights.

questions.question_text: A patient develops low mood and poor sleep
questions.explanation: Beta blockers have been consistently associated with depression and sleep disturbances.

questions.question_text: May cause mania and delirium
questions.explanation: Levodopa can cause psychiatric symptoms including hypomania and psychosis, which are dose limiting side effects.

options.text: SPECT scan showing loss of functional dopaminergic neuron terminals in the hypothalamus
SPECT scans showing hypoperfusion of the frontal lobe
MRI showing focal white matter lesions
MRI with medial temporal lobe atrophy
LP with raised white cell count
SPECT scan showing hypoperfusion of occipital area

correct_answers.text: MRI showing focal white matter lesions

questions.explanation: Multiple sclerosis typically shows discrete white matter abnormalities on MRI.

questions.question_text: Patient with slow onset dementia in multiple cognitive domains

options.text: SPECT scan showing loss of functional dopaminergic neuron terminals in the hypothalamus
SPECT scans showing hypoperfusion of the frontal lobe
MRI showing focal white matter lesions
MRI with medial temporal lobe atrophy
LP with raised white cell count

correct_answers.text: MRI with medial temporal lobe atrophy

questions.question_text: Patient with change in personality and becoming disinhibited

options.text: SPECT scan showing loss of functional dopaminergic neuron terminals in the hypothalamus
SPECT scans showing hypoperfusion of the frontal lobe
MRI showing focal white matter lesions

correct_answer.text: SPECT scans showing hypoperfusion of the frontal lobe

correct_answers.text: SPECT scans showing hypoperfusion of the frontal lobe

questions.explanation: Frontotemporal dementia shows hypoperfusion of the frontal lobe on functional imaging.

questions.question_text: Patient suffering from visual hallucinations made worse by neuroleptics

options.text: SPECT scan showing loss of functional dopaminergic neuron terminals in the hypothalamus
SPECT scans showing hypoperfusion of the frontal lobe
MRI showing focal white matter lesions
MRI with medial temporal lobe atrophy
LP with raised white cell count
SPECT scan showing hypoperfusion of occipital area

correct_answer.text: SPECT scan showing hypoperfusion of occipital area

correct_answers.text: SPECT scan showing hypoperfusion of occipital area

questions.explanation: Dementia with Lewy bodies shows occipital hypoperfusion on SPECT, and symptoms worsen with antipsychotics.

questions.question_text: You see a middle-aged woman who you have been treating for depression with duloxetine. However she confides in you that she is having intrusive thoughts of an aggressive and sexual nature.
questions.explanation: Sertraline is effective for obsessions and ruminations of OCD; combination of an SNRI and TCA is not advisable.

questions.question_text: You're treating a young woman with post-partum depression with fluoxetine. She has not improved in the last 8 weeks. She is not currently breastfeeding.
questions.explanation: NICE guidelines recommend switch to another SSRI, mirtazepine, reboxetine or lofepramine; if not breastfeeding, SSRI or TCA could be options.

questions.question_text: You're treating a man with citalopram. He has not responded well and his most problematic symptom is severe insomnia.
questions.explanation: Mirtazapine can be considered due to its sedative effects by acting on H1 receptors.

questions.question_text: You want to compare the effectiveness of Drug X versus drug Y
questions.explanation: Randomised controlled trials are used to study effectiveness and safety profile of medications and have the best evidence in clinical trials.

questions.question_text: You want to find out if people taking drug X have more side effects than people taking drug Y
questions.explanation: Prospective cohort studies are best suited to assess side effect profiles of medication, as RCTs may be considered unethical for this purpose.

questions.question_text: You want to find out about the experiences of patients taking drug X vs Drug Y.
questions.explanation: Patients experiences can be studied using a qualitative study.

questions.question_text: Your consultant wants to find out how many patients are currently being prescribed drug X and how many are being prescribed drug Y.
questions.explanation: Cross sectional study gives the number of patients currently on the medication at the time of the study.

questions.question_text: A guideline is published to suggest that Drug X should be used as first line and your consultant wants to know whether this guideline is being followed.
questions.explanation: Studying whether current practice adheres to guidelines is an audit.

questions.question_text: From the options above, choose interpersonal “Curative factors” in a group.
questions.explanation: Yalom identified 11 curative factors in groups including cohesiveness and universality along with others.

questions.question_text: Bion’s factors which affect group therapy
questions.explanation: Bion identified factors that hinder group work including dependence and fight-flight response; groups hold basic assumptions of dependence and fight-flight.

questions.question_text: Factors seen facilitating communication in a psychodynamic group
questions.explanation: Free-floating discussion and interpreting transference are important processes in psychodynamic groups.

questions.question_text: Angelman syndrome
questions.explanation: In Angelman syndrome there is paroxysmal laughing and ataxic gait along with microcephaly and severe learning disability.

questions.question_text: William syndrome
questions.explanation: Children with Williams syndrome are highly sociable but also susceptible to significant social anxiety.

questions.question_text: Lesch Nyhan Syndrome
questions.explanation: Self-mutilating behaviors such as lip and finger biting are a striking feature of Lesch Nyhan Syndrome.

questions.question_text: Fragile X syndrome
questions.explanation: Fragile X syndrome features macroorchidism and shyness with social anxiety.

questions.question_text: You want to collect information about the opinion of people from different professional backgrounds
questions.explanation: Grounded theory is a systematic qualitative research methodology emphasizing generation of theory from data. Purposive sampling involves selecting participants to cover a range of relevant perspectives.

questions.question_text: How will you know that you have enough data?
questions.explanation: Data saturation occurs when further interviews do not add new information.

questions.question_text: You decide that you want to get the opinions of social workers and nurses and analyse them separately
questions.explanation: Triangulation refers to collecting information from different sources to corroborate data.

questions.question_text: You decide that you need an independent person to review the analysis of your data
questions.explanation: Investigator triangulation requires more than one investigator to collect and analyze data so that findings emerge through consensus.

questions.question_text: Two observer rated scales to monitor response to treatment in a woman with a 6 week old baby diagnosed to have depression

options.text: Edinburgh post natal depression rating scale

questions.explanation: HAM-D and MADRS are two observer rating scales used to monitor changes in depression.

questions.question_text: One scale to screen a post partum woman for depression

options.text: Edinburgh post natal depression rating scale

correct_answer.text: Edinburgh post natal depression rating scale

correct_answers.text: Edinburgh post natal depression rating scale

questions.explanation: The Edinburgh postnatal depression rating scale has been specifically designed to screen for depression in the postnatal period.

questions.question_text: One scale to assess extrapyramidal side effects

options.text: Edinburgh post natal depression rating scale

questions.explanation: Simpson Angus scale is used to assess extrapyramidal side effects.

questions.question_text: An 18-year-old man presents to the A&E with vivid visual hallucinations, dilated pupils, and increased appetite.
questions.explanation: Effects of cannabis intoxication include euphoria, relaxation, hallucinations, hilarity, increased appetite and glazed eyes with large pupils.

questions.question_text: A 24 year old man presents with dilated pupils, reduced appetite, auditory hallucinations, insomnia and irritability.
questions.explanation: Effects of amphetamine intoxication include increased alertness, pulse rate and blood pressure, and feeling of high energy. Patients present with dilated pupils, insomnia, loss of appetite and irritability.

questions.question_text: A 34 year old man presenting with slurred speech, incoordination of movements, and nystagmus.
questions.explanation: Acute alcohol and benzodiazepine intoxication can present with similar signs including incoordination, slurred speech, ocular signs, and confusion.

questions.question_text: The following disorder results due to deletion of the chromosome of maternal origin
questions.explanation: Angelman syndrome is due to the microdeletion in the long arm of the maternally derived chromosome 15, characterised by ataxia, epilepsy, paroxysm of laughter, absence of speech, microcephaly, severe LD, and behavior problems.

questions.question_text: An infarct in which region leads to an increased rate of depression:
questions.explanation: MRI-documented infarcts in hippocampus, basal ganglia and frontal areas have been classically associated with post stroke depression.

questions.question_text: The common side effect of clonidine does not include
questions.explanation: Uncommon CNS side effects of clonidine include insomnia, anxiety, depression, nightmares and hallucinations.

questions.question_text: The proportion of patients with brain tumours presenting with psychiatric symptoms include
questions.explanation: Two of the larger series of cerebral tumor patients report a percentage of 78% & 52%.

questions.question_text: Tests for measuring continuous variables does not include
questions.explanation: Chi-square and logistic regression deal with binomial theory; t-tests, ANOVA, correlation, and regression deal with continuous variables.

questions.question_text: Which of the following personality disorders is most commonly seen in patients over the age of 60 who commit suicide?
questions.explanation: Personality disorder or personality trait accentuation was present in 44% of older suicides, with anankastic or anxious traits the most frequent. Personality factors, as well as depression, are important risk factors for suicide in older people.

questions.question_text: The following is not a scale for depression
questions.explanation: The YBOCS was designed in order to provide a rating scale which would be a measure of the severity of symptoms of OCD. Rating scales, Freeman & Graham, p-30

questions.question_text: The risk of suicide after 1 year of self harming is
questions.explanation: Owen et al in 2002 in their systematic review concluded that the risk of suicide following DSH as between 0.5-2% after 1 year and above 5% after 9 years. Companion to Psychiatric Studies, 7th edn, pg 678

questions.question_text: Clozapine is indicated if there is no response to
questions.explanation: Offer clozapine to people with schizophrenia whose illness has not responded adequately to treatment despite the sequential use of adequate doses of at least two different antipsychotic drugs. At least one of the drugs should be a non-clozapine second-generation antipsychotic. Nice guidelines for Schizophrenia, March 2009

questions.question_text: You are treating a patient with depression by fluoxetine without response. Subsequently there is a partial response to amitriptyline. The next line of treatment is
questions.explanation: CBT along with antidepressants increases the effectiveness of treatment of depression. Increasing the dose and augmentation are other options that can be considered. NICE guidelines for depression, 2009

questions.question_text: The last stage according to Prochaska and Diclemente model of change of behavior is
questions.explanation: In the last stage (maintenance stage) the new behaviors such as abstinence are perpetuated. Handbook of Alcoholism, 2000, Zernig et al, P-99-100

questions.question_text: Following is an example of Nominal data
questions.explanation: These variables, also called "attribute variables" or "categorical variables," classify observations into a small number of categories. A good rule of thumb is that an individual observation of a nominal variable is usually a word, not a number. Examples of nominal variables include sex (the possible values are male or female), genotype (values are AA, Aa, or aa), or ankle condition (values are normal, sprained, torn ligament, or broken). Nominal variables are often used to divide individuals up into classes, so that other variables may be compared among the classes. In the comparison of head width in male vs. female isopods, the isopods are classified by sex, a nominal variable, and the measurement variable head width is compared between the sexes.

questions.question_text: The mechanism of action of Modafinil includes
questions.explanation: Modafinil activates hypocretin producing neurons thus useful in Narcolepsy. Modafinil is reported to act by alpha 1 agonism accounting for its alertness. Kaplan & saddock, 10 edn, p-1099

questions.question_text: You are using a motivational interview approach on a patient with Hypochondriasis. Which of the following is an approach that should be used?

options.text: Making the patient feel that you understand them
Attempt to amplify the ambivalence regarding change
Making the patient feel that you believe them

correct_answer.text: Attempt to amplify the ambivalence regarding change

correct_answers.text: Attempt to amplify the ambivalence regarding change

questions.explanation: Motivational Interviewing is a client-centred approach to enhancing motivation for change. The main strategy is to explore and amplify ambivalence regarding change rather than attempt to confront or persuade the client. Amplifying resistance amplifies the person's cognitive dissonance, which thereby motivates the person to try to minimize resistance, such as by developing a strong commitment to engage in treatment to overcome his or her problems. A variety of well described techniques are used to promote this process (e.g., rolling with resistance, developing discrepancy, and reinforcing self-efficacy statements; see Miller & Rollnick, 2002). The goal is to help the patient to become his or her own advocate for change by decreasing ambivalence and increasing motivation. McKay & Bouman (2008) Enhancing Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy for Monosymptomatic Hypochondriasis With Motivational Interviewing: Three Case Illustrations. Journal of Cognitive Psychotherapy: An International Quarterly 22(2):154-166

questions.question_text: The most common side effect that you would discuss with a patient when prescribing cyproterone acetate is?
questions.explanation: The side effects of cyproterone acetate is gynaecomastia, thromboembolic phenomena, fatigue and depression. Companion to Psychiatric Studies, 7 edn, p-765

questions.question_text: The most common neurological side effect of Fluoxetine is
questions.explanation: Fluoxetine is the SSRI that is most likely to cause headache. The incidence is 18-20%. Kaplan & Saddock, Synopsis of Psychiatry, 10 edn, p-1088

questions.question_text: The database that provides systematic coverage of the psychological literature from the 1800s to the present is
The test that is used in patients who are diagnosed with mild dementia in order to assess their ability to drive is
questions.explanation: A special driving assessment (commonly referred to as Mobility Driving Test) is used to determine the driver's competency and ability in the areas of concentration, perception, attention, and/or judgment. The test could be appropriate if a medical diagnosis of mild dementia is given.

questions.question_text: A 30 year old man has been suffering from schizophrenia asks you about the percentage of people who discontinue medication during the first 18 months of treatment
questions.explanation: Medication discontinuation is a major problem in the treatment of first-episode patients; The CATIE study found that 74 percent of patients discontinued the antipsychotic medication before 18 months (1061 of the 1432 patients who received at least one dose): 64 percent of those assigned to olanzapine, 75 percent of those assigned to perphenazine, 82 percent of those assigned to quetiapine, 74 percent of those assigned to risperidone, and 79 percent of those assigned to ziprasidone. Lieberman et al., Effectiveness of Antipsychotic Drugs in Patients with Chronic Schizophrenia. NEJM. 2005, 353:1209-1223.

questions.question_text: You are seeing the parents of a 26 year old gentleman currently under your care. He has been diagnosed with Schizophrenia and his parents want to know his prognosis. What type of schizophrenia has the best prognosis out of the following
questions.explanation: Factors associated with good prognosis are: paranoid type, female, married, abrupt onset, family history of affective disorder, lack of negative and cognitive symptoms. Lieberman et al 1993 Current opinion in Psychiatry.

questions.question_text: The following is more accurate about rates of recidivism in adolescents as compared to adults

options.text: Adolescents had higher rate of recidivism for non sexual offences
Adolescents had a higher rate of recidivism for sexual offences as adults
Adolescents had a rate of recidivism for sexual offences that is similar to adults
Adolescents had a lower rate of recidivism for sexual offences as adults
Recidivism rates for non sexual offences were similar in adults

correct_answer.text: Adolescents had a higher rate of recidivism for sexual offences as adults

correct_answers.text: Adolescents had a higher rate of recidivism for sexual offences as adults

questions.explanation: The juvenile non sexual offenders had higher rates of adult recidivism for all other types of offences. Juvenile sexual offenders adjudicated for a sexual offence had a significantly higher rate of recidivism for sexual offences as adults than did the comparison group but rearrest rates for sexual offences were low in both groups. Sipe et al, Criminal justice and behaviour 1998,25,109.

questions.question_text: Which correlation co-efficient demonstrates an inverse relationship between two variables?
questions.explanation: The strength or magnitude of the relationship between the two variables is expressed by a statistic known as the CORRELATION COEFFICIENT, which varies from -1 (perfect negative relationship or inverse correlation), through 0 (no relationship) to +1 (perfect positive relationship).

questions.question_text: Which of the following cognitive function is less impaired in patients with schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: Language, motor and visuospatial functions are less consistently impaired. Bilder, R. M., Goodman, R. S., Robinson, D., et al (2000) Neuropsychology of first-episode schizophrenia: initial characterisation and clinical correlates. American Journal of Psychiatry, 157, 549-559.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a significant variable predictor of Sexual Offence Recidivism in Offenders with Intellectual Disabilities
questions.explanation: Significant variables were allowances made by staff, antisocial attitude, poor relationship with mother, denial of crime, sexual abuse in childhood, erratic attendance and poor response to treatment. William R. Lindsay, Susanne F. Elliot and Arlene Astell, Predictors of Sexual Offence Recidivism in Offenders with Intellectual Disabilities. Journal of Applied Research in Intellectual Disabilities 2004, 17(4); 299 - 305.

questions.question_text: The following is commonly seen in a patient with anorexia nervosa
questions.explanation: In a community sample of 214 women with anorexia nervosa, the common medical findings included; anemia, 38.6%; leukocytopenia, 34.4%; hyponatremia, 19.7%; hypokalemia, 19.7%; bradycardia, 41.3%; hypotension, 16.1%; hypothermia, 22.4%; elevation of alanine aminotransferase concentration, 12.2%; osteopenia, 51.7%; osteoporosis, 34.6%; and primary amenorrhea, 14.8%. Miller et al. Common Findings in outpatients with Anorexia Nervosa. Arch Intern Med. 2005;165:561-566.

questions.question_text: Autism is most likely to be associated with which of the following:
questions.explanation: Hyperactivity is common with autism. Goodman & Scott, Child Psychiatry, 2002, pg 43.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an actuarial risk assessment instrument to assess risk of sexual offending
questions.explanation: The Sex Offender Risk Appraisal Guide (SORAG) is to assess risk of sexual recidivism. Hare Psychopathy Checklist Revised (PCL-R), Historical Clinical Risk (HCR-20), and Violence Risk Appraisal Guide (VRAG) are actuarial risk instruments for violent recidivism. Spousal Assault Risk Assessment Guide (SARA) is for spousal assault risk. Forensic Psychiatry - Risk Assessment Instruments.

questions.question_text: The antidepressant of choice in the treatment of depression in a patient with cerebral palsy is
questions.explanation: Fluoxetine is licenced for use in children & adolescents. There are case reports of use of fluoxetine in treating depression in cerebral palsy. Cerebral palsy and juvenile-onset bipolar disorder. A preliminary report, European Child & Adolescent Psychiatry, 11:134-137 (2002).

questions.question_text: The ideal value for kappa is
questions.explanation: Kappa is a measure of inter-rater reliability. If the raters are in complete agreement then Kappa = 1. If there is no agreement among the raters (other than what would be expected by chance) then Kappa = 0. Companion to Psychiatric Studies, 7th edn, pg 189.

questions.question_text: A 36 year old man with opioid dependence wishes to have opioid detoxification, he has tendency to suffer from low blood pressure and he is not keen on using opiates. Which of the following would you use?
questions.explanation: Buprenorphine or methadone are first-line but are opiates. Lofexidine and clonidine are alpha-2 agonists; lofexidine is less likely to cause hypotension compared to clonidine hence this could be the choice if the patient prefers not to use opiates. NICE guidelines, 2007.

questions.question_text: The preferred type of sampling used to recruit participants in a study involving drug users is
questions.explanation: Snowball sampling is often used in hidden populations which are difficult for researchers to access; example populations would be drug users. Goodman, L.A. (1961). "Snowball sampling". Annals of Mathematical Statistics 32: 148-170.

questions.question_text: The following is helpful in differentiating dissociative seizures from true seizures
questions.explanation: Dissociative seizures are usually more than 2 minutes, gradual in onset, with occasional pelvic thrusting which is rare in epileptic seizures, and severe tongue biting is very rare in dissociative seizures. Lishman's Organic Psychiatry, 4th edn, pg 359.

questions.question_text: Which of the following can cause both hyperglycaemia and dyslipidaemia
questions.explanation: The relative risk of glucose intolerance or diabetes mellitus, hyperlipidaemia and hyperleptinaemia is highest for clozapine and olanzapine, moderately high for quetiapine, rather low for risperidone and lowest for ziprasidone. Adverse Metabolic Effects Associated with Atypical Antipsychotics: Literature Review and Clinical Implications, Drugs, Volume 64, Number 7, 2004, pp. 701-723.

questions.question_text: A woman lost her mother recently. A feature which would suggest depression rather than a grief reaction are:
questions.explanation: The symptoms of retardation and global loss of self esteem are seldom present in uncomplicated grief. Shorter Oxford Textbook of Psychiatry, 5th edn, pg 170.

questions.question_text: The risk of heart failure in patients with coronary artery disease and depression compared to those with coronary artery disease without depression is
questions.explanation: The risk of heart failure in patients with CAD and depression is 16.4 per 100 and the risk of HF in patients with CAD and without depression is 3.6 per 100. May et al. Depression After Coronary Artery Disease Is Associated With Heart Failure. J Am Coll Cardiol, 2009; 53:1440-1447.

questions.question_text: Empathy Skills are most likely to be delayed in

options.text: A deaf child of hearing parents
A hearing child of deaf parents
A hearing child with one deaf parent
A deaf child of deaf parents
A hearing child adopted for 6 months by deaf parents

correct_answer.text: A deaf child of hearing parents

correct_answers.text: A deaf child of hearing parents

questions.explanation: Deaf children outperform both deaf children of hearing parents and hearing children on false-belief tasks, probably due to early exposure to visual perspective-taking (sign-language). Deaf children with hearing parents show delayed theory of mind acquisition. This shows that language has an important role to play in acquisition of Theory of Mind. Peterson & Siegal, Mind & Language.

questions.question_text: The mechanism of Psychotropic related QT prolongation is
questions.explanation: Antipsychotics appear to share the ability to antagonize the rapid component of the delayed rectifier IKr which results in variable lengthening of the action potential, delayed repolarization and QT prolongation. Taylor DM. Antipsychotics and QT prolongation. Acta Psychiatr Scand 2003:107:85-95.

questions.question_text: To diagnose schizotypal disorder according to ICD-10, the following criteria needs to be fulfilled.
questions.explanation: The typical features of schizotypal disorder should have been present, continuously or episodically, for at least 2 years. ICD-10, 1992.

questions.question_text: A patient who has recently completed an inpatient detoxification from opiates would like to be prescribed something that will help to prevent relapse. Which of the following would be the most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Buprenorphine and methadone have been recommended as first line in the maintenance treatment of opiate dependence. Naltrexone is used in the abstinence based treatments to prevent relapse, not as first line. NICE guidelines, 2007.

questions.question_text: The following is a feature of Progressive supranuclear palsy:

options.text: Lateral gaze problems are an early feature

questions.explanation: In supranuclear palsy the onset is usually in the 6th decade; ocular symptoms affect the vertical plane involving downward gaze; there are frequent backwards falls and neurofibrillary tangles are seen in the basal ganglia, brainstem and cerebellar nuclei. Bradyphrenia (slowed thinking) is common. Lishman's Organic Psychiatry, 4th edn, pg 776.

questions.question_text: Concerning Naltrexone, which of the following is true;

options.text: There are no risks with discontinuation of Naltrexone
Motivation of patient is not needed
Naltrexone is better than methadone in relapse prevention
It is not cost effective for opioid dependence
Evidence for the effectiveness of naltrexone as a treatment for relapse prevention in opioid misusers has not been conclusive

correct_answer.text: Evidence for the effectiveness of naltrexone as a treatment for relapse prevention in opioid misusers has not been conclusive

correct_answers.text: Evidence for the effectiveness of naltrexone as a treatment for relapse prevention in opioid misusers has not been conclusive

questions.explanation: Evidence of effectiveness of Naltrexone as a treatment for relapse prevention in opioid dependence has been inconclusive. Individuals in abstinence programmes need to be highly motivated, are to be fully informed of the potential adverse effects and benefits of treatment. Naltrexone treatment has been found by NICE to be a cost effective treatment strategy in aiding abstinence from opiates. Maudsley guidelines, 10 edn, p-314.

questions.question_text: Which of the following would you see abnormal language development in?
questions.explanation: Deficits in language development and difficulty using language to communicate ideas are among the principal criteria for diagnosing autistic disorder. Synopsis of Psychiatry, 10th edn, pg 1194.

questions.question_text: The following clinical symptom is more suggestive of serotonin syndrome rather than Lithium toxicity
questions.explanation: The GI symptoms of Lithium toxicity include vomiting, abdominal pain and dryness of mouth. Hyperreflexia is more suggestive of serotonin syndrome. Kaplan & Sadock, Synopsis of Psychiatry, 10 edn, p-1060 & 1089.

questions.question_text: A 23 year old woman has features of hypomania and she is also breast feeding her baby. The best treatment option for treatment of hypomania is
questions.explanation: Antipsychotics apart from clozapine can be used in breastfeeding mothers but all the others mentioned here should be avoided if possible. NICE guidelines, The management of bipolar disorder in adults, children and adolescents, in primary and secondary care. 2006.

questions.question_text: An 18 year old male presents with diaphoresis, agitation, tachycardia and dilated pupils. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Amphetamine causes non life threatening effects such as pupillary dilation, excessive sweating, agitation and tachycardia in addition to life threatening effects (MI, severe hypertension, ischaemic colitis). Synopsis of Psychiatry, 10th edn, pg 410.

questions.question_text: Smoking in a pregnant lady can lead to the following in the child
questions.explanation: Smoking in pregnancy is associated with ADHD and behaviour problems including conduct disorders and antisocial behaviour in the child. Langley K et al. BMC Psychiatry 2007;7:26.

questions.question_text: The symptom that is suggestive of hepatic encephalopathy in a patient in the ICU is
questions.explanation: Hepatic encephalopathy is suggested by Asterixis and can occur in chronic liver failure and acute fulminant hepatic failure. Asterixis is an abnormal tremor consisting of involuntary jerking movements, especially in the hands also called flapping tremor. Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, vol 2, 15 edn, p-2495.

questions.question_text: What does PECO mean?
questions.explanation: The acronym PICO or PECO provides precision and focus to identify problems in health care delivery. It helps in decision making. PICO or PECO stands for P-patient or population, E-exposure or I-intervention, C-comparison & O-outcome. Evidence-based healthcare and public health: how to make decisions, John Armstrong Muir Gray & Erica Ison, p-343, 2008.

questions.question_text: What is the standard error of mean if population is 16 and standard deviation is 8
questions.explanation: The standard error of the mean (SEM) is estimated by the sample standard deviation divided by the square root of the sample size: SEM = s/√n. Here s=8, n=16 so SEM = 8/4 = 2. Everitt, B.S. (2003) The Cambridge Dictionary of Statistics, CUP.
